_README: These are DRAFT catalog entries. Do NOT load this file from the server. Review each entry, verify the firmware links and brick-risk claims, and promote to catalog.json one at a time. All entries here are LLM-drafted (not founder-verified) — provenance is set to 'community-reported' but you should confirm against the linked sources before promoting. Drafted 2026-05-04.

candidates.name: Philips Hue Go (1st gen)
candidates.notes: Portable Hue lamp with battery. Pairs with Zigbee2MQTT or Home Assistant. Programmable color animations are the killer use case for ambient/breathing apps.

candidates.name: Amazon Echo Dot (2nd gen)
candidates.notes: Cheap on eBay since voice-assistant fatigue. Reverse-engineering attempts exist; bricks are common. Consider as 'amplified speaker via aux-out only' for low-risk use.

candidates.name: ESP32 DevKit-C
candidates.notes: Default ESP32 board for tinkering. Wi-Fi + BLE, runs MicroPython or Arduino. Common in DIY ambient displays, sensor relays, custom IoT projects.

candidates.name: Kobo Clara HD
candidates.notes: 6-inch e-ink reader, Linux underneath. Telnet/SSH via 'developer mode' file. KOReader and InkBox provide custom OSes. Less common than Kindle but more open.

candidates.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
candidates.notes: Smaller than Pi 4B, lower power. Good for projects that need to be embedded/hidden. Reasonable Wi-Fi. Slightly slow CPU but usually enough.

candidates.name: Anker Soundcore Mini (BT speaker)
candidates.notes: Common cheap BT speaker. No firmware hack — paired with an ESP32 or Pi as the audio source for ambient drone soundscapes. Listed because the eBay-search use case is real.

candidates.name: Olimex ESP32-POE
candidates.notes: ESP32 with PoE Ethernet. Single cable for power and network — good for wall-mounted displays/sensors with no wall-warts.

candidates.name: TP-Link TL-WR841N (router)
candidates.notes: Cheap consumer router. OpenWrt support varies by hardware revision (v8+ are more constrained). Listed for projects needing a tiny Linux box with Wi-Fi where Pi is overkill.

candidates.name: LeapFrog LeapPad 2
candidates.notes: Kid-oriented Android-derived tablet. SAFETY NOTE: handheld + llm-inferred = brick-risk score will be stripped from output by the safety rule. Listed because the 'kid coding station' use case occasionally surfaces this.

candidates.name: iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit
candidates.notes: Not a hackable device per se. Listed as a meta-recommendation for when proposals require disassembly. Consider deleting if catalog focus tightens.
